structural.name: Restore confirm
structural.why: UX-I-01 (Critical) — the 'All changes' timestamp shipped labelled 'Jump to 14:32' and called composer.history.restoreEntry straight from the click; restoreEntry empties redo and does undoStack.slice(0, index+1) (HistoryManager.ts:757-775). The word 'Jump' promised navigation and performed an irreversible edit. Placed where 163:213 sits on 163:167 — directly under the panel chrome — because one restore contract means one drawing of it.

parts.s: Restore to 14:32?
This rewinds the project to Added block at 14:32. It permanently discards 12 later changes and everything you can currently redo. Some of that work has not been saved yet.

structural.name: Restore confirm
structural.why: UX-I-02 (Critical) — 'Restore this point' fires into the same truncating restore with no confirmation (TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:264-268 → HistoryTab.tsx:195-201 → restoreEntry), while the identical operation on a named version two clicks away shows a confirm band. Placed under the drawer's own note, which already says 'Nothing is written until Restore' — this is the button honouring it.

structural.name: First-hit notice
structural.why: UX-I-05 (Major) — the once-only announcement when the 100-step cap is first hit. HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING (events.ts:133) has zero emitters and zero listeners, so this is design-ahead of the code and the board is named accordingly.

parts.s: Undo now only reaches back 100 steps. Save a version to keep this point for good.

structural.name: History boundary
structural.why: UX-I-05 (Major) — undo is capped at 100 and trimHistory() shifts entries off the front with no emit (HistoryManager.ts:613-629; config.ts:108), so the list simply stops going back. The boundary terminates the list, which is why it is inserted immediately before the spacer rather than floated. NOT drawn on 163:269 'pruned-notice': that board states the VERSION store's 50-item rule, a different store with a different boundary, and reusing it would re-create the exact conflation UX-I-09 exists to break.

structural.name: Clear confirm
structural.why: UX-I-07 (Major) — 'Clear' wipes the entire undo stack and the confirm is the same button re-labelled 'Clear all', which never states the consequence. The cost is now in both the sentence and the primary's own label.

structural.name: Undo unavailable notice
structural.why: UX-I-15 (Major, HALF STALE) — the half that is stale is NOT drawn. useComposerInit.ts:705-716 has listened to HISTORY_UNRECORDED since de36af334 (2026-09-04) and already disables Undo, so the switch-off is no longer silent. What survives, and all this band claims, is that the disabled action is ANONYMOUS: the label is engine-supplied (noteUnrecordedAction's `label` argument, 'said the way the toast will say it'; BaseBindingManager.ts:106 passes 'binding a field to content') and nothing renders it.

structural.name: Saves overflow menu
structural.why: UX-I-08 (not a gap-C finding — same reason as UX-I-12). Import defaults to MERGE and the destructive mode is a separate, explicitly-named row: importVersions(file, clearExisting=false) already has that default. Drawn as an ABSOLUTE popover, not a stack insert: the board's spacer measures 171 and the menu is 244 tall, and a menu opened from the panel header's ⋯ is a floating surface anyway — it costs the stack nothing.
